reason: No prior evidence is cited to support any of the key premises. The claims about Ni-induced interlayer formation, its role as a diffusion barrier, its effect on phase separation and void suppression, and its stability under irradiation are all presented without reference to specific experimental or theoretical studies.
premises: Ni addition forms a stable, thin W–Ni–Cu intermetallic interlayer at W–Cu interfaces during powder processing
The interlayer enhances interfacial wettability and acts as a diffusion barrier
The interlayer reduces differential diffusion-driven phase separation and prevents void nucleation
The stabilized interface minimizes thermal impedance, improving thermal conductivity
The interlayer remains effective under service conditions up to ~900°C and moderate irradiation (~10 dpa)
